items.abstract: <jats:p>This article introduces a family of rough path-dependent volatility (RPDV) models that encompass a wide range of modeling two major empirical features of volatility: its rough behavior and its path dependence. After presenting it in its general form and its connections to other existing models in the literature, we provide a Markovian multi-factor approximation of this family of RPDV models, building upon the works of Abi Jaber (2019). Then, our analysis focuses on some specifications of RPDV models interpretable from an economic point of view, leading to the formulation of different hypotheses about both asset price and volatility formation mechanisms.</jats:p>
title: Rough Path-Dependent Volatility Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper introduces the Decoupled Exponential Path Algebra, a feature-explicit, dimensionally contractive mathematical framework designed for high-dimensional continuous stream processing and sequence learning. Traditional path-based topological transformations, such as the classical path signature and the Exponentially Weighted Signature, suffer from a severe combinatorial curse of dimensionality that renders high-order feature extraction computationally prohibitive when analysing large channel dimensions. The proposed architecture resolves this fundamental bottleneck through a two-stage Decouple-then-Couple paradigm. In the accumulation stage, the global noncommutative trajectory representation is completely factorised across three independent axes: low-rank orthogonal spatial projections, a multi-scale spectral memory bank capturing parallel temporal attenuation regimes, and an invariant tiered truncation strategy. This factorisation maps continuous non-linear path integration into a system of discrete linear recurrent states. By proving a strict affine associativity condition over the cross-temporal transitions, we show that long historical contexts can be evaluated concurrently in logarithmic time complexity via a parallel associative scan. In the output stage, a data-driven Adaptive Coupling Layer is introduced as a post-processing snapshot operation over the spatial-spectral manifold, dynamically reconstructing lost cross-channel structures without re-entering the temporal loop. Analytically, we establish rigorous topological guarantees by proving the global Lipschitz continuity of the transform under the variation metric topology, deriving explicit bounds that quantify the factorial decay of residual truncation information leakage, and proving a universal functional approximation theorem over compact rough path manifolds. Furthermore, we define a decoupled tree-like equivalence relation to completely characterise the geometric filtration properties of the mapping, introducing a universal recoverability theorem which rigorously demonstrates that the filtered cross-channel properties (such as global Lévy areas) are provably recoverable up to an arbitrary uniform error tolerance over the compact quotient space. Together, DEPA provides a scalable, mathematically rigorous, and highly parallelisable paradigm for continuous-time sequence analysis.</jats:p>
title: Decoupled Exponential Path Algebras: Geometric Recoverability and Scalable Rough Path Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>This presentation introduces the rough path-dependent volatility model (RPDVM). After defining the model and its different components, the presentation focuses on various specifications of the RPDVM that already exist in the literature. Finally, a Markovian approximation of the model is presented.</jats:p>
